A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FairLocator study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title and appendix organization.

before.justification: v2 reports original VLM evaluations, a human geolocation study, and supplementary experiments on image dates, private photographs, rural scenes, prompting, and sample size.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds landmark evaluation, a CLIP comparison, and further analyses of geolocation errors.

M1.justification: The FairLocator querying pipeline, geolocation prompt, EXIF removal, response format, and answer matching remain unchanged. CLIP is introduced as a comparison method; the PDFs do not establish a revision to the proposed pipeline.

E1.justification: Section 5.1 adds a distinct landmark scenario using 50 Google Street View images of UNESCO heritage sites across five UN regional groups. The original Depth/Breadth coverage and existing temporal, private-photo, Chinatown, and rural scenarios remain.

E2.justification: Appendix B.3 adds evaluated zero-shot CLIP (ViT-B/32), with a random baseline in Table 18. Existing VLM and human comparisons remain. Section 4.1 also newly reports that Phi-4-Multimodal returned 'Unknown' for every city query and was excluded from the tabulated comparisons.

E3.justification: New supplementary protocols include sampling ten landmarks per UN group, CLIP retrieval among 111 candidate city names, and distance scoring with 100 km and 1000 km thresholds. Existing query, retry, and matching procedures remain; newly disclosed decoding parameters do not establish changed earlier settings or reruns.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands error analysis through continent confusion matrices, country-level distance bins, and selected-city comparisons separating nearby errors from distant failures (Section 4.3; Appendices A.3–A.4 and B.4). It also adds the landmark memorization check. Earlier sample-size, rural, CoT, and o3 analyses are retained under reorganized headings.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three responses per image for the main evaluation and retain the same standard-deviation comparison in the sample-size analysis (v2 Appendix D; v3 B.1). No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run reporting is introduced.

E6.justification: All eight v2 tables retain their numerical contents in corresponding v3 tables. Substantial additional results include four confusion matrices, distance-bin results, GPT-4o landmark city accuracy of 0.64 (Table 7), and CLIP accuracy of 17.8% against a 0.9% random baseline (Table 18). These are newly reported results, not improvements to retained scores.

T1.justification: Appendix A.4 newly defines a piecewise distance score: two points within 100 km, one for 100–1000 km, and zero beyond 1000 km, according to the captions. Existing entropy and distance definitions remain unchanged; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about FairLocator, geographic performance disparities, preference for prominent cities, and privacy risks. The new title emphasizes an existing wealth-related bias claim without changing its scientific scope.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning partial geographic awareness during errors, rural explanations for landmark failures, and the contributions of alignment, reasoning, and world knowledge in the CLIP comparison. Appendix B.4 motivates distinguishing error severity. Existing limitations concerning bias causes and geographic coverage remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly discloses temperature 1.0 except LLaVA at 0.2, and top_p 1.0 except Gemini at 0.95. Appendix B.3 specifies CLIP's backbone and maximum-similarity selection among 111 city names. Reported code and coordinate-release arrangements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including Ramrakhiyani et al. (2025), VisBias, FairGamer, CLIP, and Phi-4, and revises citations for the evaluated model versions. These are limited additions and corrections; the central positioning around overlooked biases in VLM geolocation remains.

P1.justification: The title and one affiliation change, an LLM-use disclosure is added, and appendices are regrouped into results, discussions, case studies, and the questionnaire. Most existing prose, including the abstract and conclusion, remains unchanged; there is no extensive rewrite of the retained narrative.

P2.justification: v3 adds substantial table displays for confusion matrices, landmarks, CLIP, and distance scores. It also groups retained Figures 3–5 onto one appendix page with shorter captions and relocates the questionnaire and case studies. Existing figure content is retained rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The added landmark and CLIP evaluations, error breakdowns, and explicit decoding parameters modestly improve evidential depth and reproducibility. Their value is limited by overinterpretation of the CLIP comparison, which does not isolate reasoning, and distance-table headers stating greater than 100 km where captions specify greater than 1000 km. These reporting weaknesses reduce, but do not outweigh, the gains.
